chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: Abu Tahir al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Isa narrated to me, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, saying: I was with Abu Abdullah

an old man entered upon him and said: 'My sons have been undutiful to me and my brothers have turned away from me.' Abu Abdullah said: 'Do you not know that the truth has a government (era/state) and the untruth also has a government? Each of them is lowly in the state of the other. Whoever is afflicted by the ease/prosperity of the untruth will be retributed for it in the state of the truth.'

key_terms.جَفَا: To turn away or become estranged
key_terms.دَوْلَة: Era, state, or period of governance/power
key_terms.عَقَّ: To be undutiful or neglectful (of parents)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'dawlah' for truth and falsehood in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) uses the concept of *dawlah* (era/state) to reassure the elder that familial estrangement is a temporary trial within the broader cosmic struggle between truth and falsehood. The Imam highlights the eschatological justice of the Qa'im's era, where the 'ease' (*rafahiyya*) enjoyed by the righteous during the dominance of falsehood will be repaid, while the oppressors will face retribution, reinforcing the Shia belief in the ultimate vindication of the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers.
